action: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (Bacs) advises a clear reduction of internet-reachable systems, the fastest possible security updates, strict access restrictions and full multi-factor authentication.
date_note: The article gives only its publication day (26 November); Bacs director Florian Schütz spoke on SRF.
exec: Switzerland's cyber office reports the first attacks on critical infrastructure supported by AI agents, with two of five confirmed cases successful; it names no victims and no attacker.
geo_basis: country (Bacs is the Swiss federal office; affected organisations not named)
plain: Switzerland's cyber office says it has seen the first attacks on critical infrastructure supported by AI agents: five confirmed cases, three on critical infrastructure, two of them successful. The source of the attacks is unclear.

sources.name: Moneycab (relaying awp, Keystone-SDA and SRF), 26 Nov 2026

summary: Moneycab reports that Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity (Bacs) has registered the first cyberattacks on critical infrastructure supported by AI agents. Per the report, five cases are confirmed, three of them affecting critical infrastructure and two of those successful. Bacs says the attackers used AI programs to search for vulnerabilities on their own; the source of the attacks is still unclear and Bacs named no victims.
title: Swiss cyber office reports first attacks on critical infrastructure using AI agents

validation.note: Corroborated by two independent publishers, Moneycab (relaying awp/Keystone-SDA/SRF) and The Hacker News (citing Bacs director Florian Schütz on SRF); each reports five confirmed cases, three on critical infrastructure and two of those successful; the Bacs original was not read.

evidence.quote: Drei dieser Angriffe betrafen demnach kritische Infrastruktur, in zwei Fällen seien die Angriffe erfolgreich gewesen.

review.note: Compared title, five/three/two figures and Bacs advice against Moneycab and The Hacker News; validation note reworded only
